name: Tu Mu
credit: Portrait: unknown artist — Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Tu Mu (AD 803–852) was a late T’ang poet, known for polished quatrains on history, travel and love.
The poems here are Herbert A. Giles’s versions in Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898), given with the poet’s name as spelled in that book.

poems.title: A Lost Love
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898)
poems.text:
Too late, alas! I came to find the lovely spring had fled.
Yet must I not regret the days of youth that now are dead;
For though the rosy buds of spring the cruel winds have laid,
Behold the clustering fruit that hangs beneath the leafy shade!

poems.title: The Old Place
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898)

poems.title: The Last Night
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898)
poems.text:
Old love would seem as though not love today;
Spell-bound by thee, my laughter dies away.
The very wax sheds sympathetic tears
And gutters sadly down till dawn appears.

poems.title: Lovers Parted
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898)
poems.text:
Across the screen the autumn moon stares coldly from the sky;
With silken fan I sit and flick the fireflies sailing by.
The night grows colder every hour, — it chills me to the heart
To watch the Spinning Maiden from the Herdboy far apart.

poems.title: I Climb to the Lo-yu Tombs Before Leaving for Wu-hsing
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: The Jade Mountain (1929)
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
Even in this good reign, how can I serve?
The lone cloud rather, the Buddhist peace . . .
Once more, before crossing river and sea,
I face the great Emperor's mountain-tomb.

poems.title: By the Purple Cliff
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: The Jade Mountain (1929)
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
On a part of a spear still unrusted in the sand
I have burnished the symbol of an ancient kingdom. . . .
Except for a wind aiding General Chou Yu,
Spring would have sealed both Ch'iao girls in Copper-Bird Palace.

poems.title: A Mooring on the Ch'in-huai River
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: The Jade Mountain (1929)
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
Mist veils the cold stream, and moonlight the sand,
As I moor in the shadow of a river-tavern,
Where girls, with no thought of a perished kingdom,
Gaily echo A Song of Courtyard Flowers.

poems.title: A Message to Han Cho the Yang-chou Magistrate
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: The Jade Mountain (1929)
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
There are faint green mountains and far green waters,
And grasses in this river region not yet faded by autumn;
And clear in the moon on the Twenty-Four Bridges,
Girls white as jade are teaching flute-music.

poems.title: A Confession
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: The Jade Mountain (1929)
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
With my wine-bottle, watching by river and lake
For a lady so tiny as to dance on my palm,
I awake, after dreaming ten years in Yang-chou,
Known as fickle, even in the Street of Blue Houses.

poems.title: In the Autumn Night
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: The Jade Mountain (1929)
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
Her candle-light is silvery on her chill bright screen.
Her little silk fan is for fireflies. . . .
She lies watching her staircase cold in the moon,
And two stars parted by the River of Heaven.

poems.title: Parting
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: The Jade Mountain (1929)
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
I

She is slim and supple and not yet fourteen,
The young spring-tip of a cardamon-spray.
On the Yang-chou Road for three miles in the breeze
Every pearl-screen is open. But there's no one like her.

II

How can a deep love seem deep love,
How can it smile, at a farewell feast?
Even the candle, feeling our sadness,
Weeps, as we do, all night long.

poems.title: The Garden of the Golden Valley
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: The Jade Mountain (1929)
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
Stories of passion make sweet dust,
Calm water, grasses unconcerned.
At sunset, when birds cry in the wind,
Petals are falling like a girl's robe long ago.

poems.title: A Night at the Tavern
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: The Jade Mountain (1929)
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
Solitary at the tavern,
I am shut in with loneliness and grief.
Under the cold lamp, I brood on the past;
I am kept awake by a lost wildgoose.
. . . Roused at dawn from a misty dream,
I read, a year late, news from home —
And I remember the moon like smoke on the river
And a fisher-boat moored there, under my door.

poems.title: 清明 (Qing ming)
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: 千家詩 (Poems of a Thousand Poets)
poems.text:
清明時節雨紛紛，路上行人慾斷魂。
借問酒家何處有，牧童遙指杏花村。

poems.title: 江南春 (Jiang nan chun)
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: 千家詩 (Poems of a Thousand Poets)
poems.text:
千里鶯啼綠映紅，水村山郭酒旗風。
南朝四百八十寺，多少樓臺煙雨中。

poems.title: 中秋月 (Zhong qiu yue)
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: 千家詩 (Poems of a Thousand Poets)
poems.text:
暮雲收盡溢清寒，銀漢無聲轉玉盤。
此生此夜不長好，明月明年何處看？

poems.title: 贈別二首·其一 (Zeng bie er shou, qi yi)
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
娉娉嫋嫋十三餘，豆蔻梢頭二月初。
春風十裏揚州路，卷上珠簾總不如。

poems.title: 贈別二首·其二 (Zeng bie er shou, qi er)
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
多情卻似總無情，唯覺樽前笑不成。
蠟燭有心還惜別，替人垂淚到天明。

poems.title: 金谷園 (Jin gu yuan)
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
繁華事散逐香塵，流水無情草自春。
日暮東風怨啼鳥，落花猶似墜樓人。

poems.title: 寄揚州韓綽判官 (Ji yang zhou han chuo pan guan)
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
青山隱隱水迢迢，秋盡江南草未凋。
二十四橋明月夜，玉人何處教吹簫？

poems.title: 遣懷 (Qian huai)
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
落魄江南載酒行，楚腰纖細掌中輕。
十年一覺揚州夢，贏得青樓薄倖名。

poems.title: 秋夕 (Qiu xi)
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
銀燭秋光冷畫屏，輕羅小扇撲流螢。
天階夜色涼如水，臥看牽牛織女星。

poems.title: 將赴吳興登樂遊原一絕 (Jiang fu wu xing deng le you yuan yi jue)
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
清時有味是無能，閒愛孤雲靜愛僧。
欲把一麾江海去，樂遊原上望昭陵。

poems.title: 赤壁 (Chi bi)
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
折戟沉沙鐵未銷，自將磨洗認前朝。
東風不與周郎便，銅雀春深鎖二喬。

poems.title: 泊秦淮 (Po qin huai)
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
煙籠寒水月籠沙，夜泊秦淮近酒家。
商女不知亡國恨，隔江猶唱後庭花。

poems.title: 旅宿 (Lü su)
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
旅館無良伴，凝情自悄然。
寒燈思舊事，斷雁警愁眠。
遠夢歸侵曉，家書到隔年。
滄江好煙月，門系釣魚船。
